extracted.intended_audience: progressive readers, women-suffrage supporters, magazine subscribers and prospective contributors to early-20th-century reform/literary periodicals (e.g., The Forerunner, The Englishwoman)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implied standards for writing, submitting, or evaluating content for The Forerunner and similar early-20th-century feminist/progressive magazines — covering acceptable topics, tone, use of evidence, and qualities prized in books and articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of conception
rubrics_metrics.description: Books/articles should show originality of conception (e.g., 'Since John Stuart Mill's essay there has been no book dealing with the whole position of women to approach it in originality of conception...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to bring genuinely new ideas or frameworks to a subject rather than rehashing familiar arguments. Originality is a primary selling/evaluative point in blurbs and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brilliancy of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are valued for 'brilliancy of exposition' — clarity, forcefulness, and stylistic excellence in presenting ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain complex ideas with clarity and rhetorical energy. Strong exposition complements originality and is repeatedly cited in favorable reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness / impact on popular thought
rubrics_metrics.description: A work's value includes its practical effect on readers and public opinion (e.g., 'the book is meant to focus all of her previous work', 'a surgical operation on the popular mind').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with an eye toward persuading or shifting common understanding; frame arguments so they can influence public practice or opinion, not just academic debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and broad appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Books and periodicals are praised for being widely readable and attractive to many (e.g., 'will be widely read and discussed', 'Thousands of women read it every week from beginning to end').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear, engaging prose and organization that invites a broad but thoughtful readership. Avoid overly technical or obscure presentation if aiming for popular uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content categories accepted by The Englishwoman
rubrics_metrics.description: The Englishwoman will publish: 'Articles dealing with the Women's Movement in England and other countries. Notes on parliamentary bills as affecting women and children. Articles on Women's Work in Professions and Trades. Sociological questions and their influence on the status of women. Stories, poems, scientific articles, and short plays. Criticisms of music, painting, sculpture, and current literature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit work that fits one of these explicit categories and that furthers the magazine's mission to 'further the Enfranchisement of Women' in a culturally literate style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to suffrage and political/social/legal/industrial matters
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The Common Cause' and 'The Woman's Journal' emphasize articles on political, social, legal and industrial matters affecting women, and act as official records of suffrage work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions directly address enfranchisement, policy developments, organizational activities, or social/legal issues affecting women; include official or documentary material where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and topicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazines prize coverage that is 'readable, timely, lively' and 'right there every time on every topic uppermost in the minds of the public' (e.g., The Forecast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch and write pieces that respond to current debates or events; use an energetic tone and highlight contemporary relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive / advanced intellectual stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals like 'The Progressive Woman' and others seek 'contributors among the cleverest of the more advanced thinkers' and aim to 'lead' rather than 'stand still.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt forward-looking, reformist perspectives; favor innovative social/political positions rather than conservative retrospection when submitting to these venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial alignment with publisher's social philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forerunner 'carries Mrs. Gilman's best and newest work; her social philosophy, her verse, satire, fiction, ethical teaching, humor, and comment. It stands for Humanness... the New Ethics, the New Economics, the New World we are to make--are making.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should resonate with the magazine's reformist, humanistic values (child-culture, home reform, new economics/ethics). Explicit alignment with the editorial mission increases acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of facts, statistics, and concrete evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The page emphasizes 'The Public Wants Facts!' and in content uses statistics and practical data (e.g., 'flies will be reduced 99 per cent. by the reduction in the number of horses...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support arguments with concrete data, examples, or empirical claims when possible. Factual grounding strengthens persuasive pieces and editorial authority; avoid unsupported assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing and moderate tone for persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Englishwoman aims to reach the cultured public 'in a convincing and moderate form' rather than partisan shrillness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt measured, reasoned argumentation to persuade skeptical or cultured readers; avoid extreme partisan rhetoric if the aim is broad influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, official, and authoritative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Woman's Journal is described as giving 'official announcements and rousing news' from the National American Woman Suffrage Association and as the only paper of its kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For journalistic submissions, include authoritative sourcing, official announcements, and comprehensive coverage of organizational activities to serve as a reliable record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable literary forms and features for bound volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher notes the bound volume contains fourteen issues (Nov 1909–Dec 1910), about 420 pages, with twelve short stories, articles, fables, verse, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contributing material intended for serial publication or inclusion in a collected volume, expect mixed-genre content (short fiction, essays, poetry) and that the publisher compiles multiple shorter pieces rather than long single works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on concrete domestic detail and practical realism in fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiction piece 'My Astonishing Dodo' foregrounds specific domestic details (weights/measures, banking, sewing machine, labelled pantry corner, exact dollar amounts) to build realism and character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, everyday details (numbers, objects, routines) to render domestic scenes believable and to reveal character through practical habits rather than abstract description alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for a cultured, literate readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Several publications on the page (Englishwoman, Forerunner, Forecast) aim at a 'cultured public' interested in letters, art, and culture and seek high literary or intellectual standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a literate register, informed references to arts/culture, and polished prose when targeting such magazines; prioritize argumentative and artistic quality over sensationalism.
